observations: A large oval head fills most of the canvas against a flat brown background; a mouth with a visible row of white teeth and a dark interior opening anchors the lower center, and two yellow-green irises sit beneath heavy black brow lines.
Hundreds of short, overlapping lines in cyan, orange, red, purple, yellow, and white cross the face in all directions, leaving no area uncovered.
A thick white outline traces the head's outer edge, separating the dense multicolor interior from the plain brown field; the right side trails into looser, darker scribbles.
reading: The face pushes toward the viewer, teeth bared and eyes fixed forward, held together by a single white boundary line. Inside that boundary, lines in every direction refuse to settle, reading as agitation rather than calm. The yellow-green irises are the one point of stillness. Brown silence surrounds everything, making the interior density feel louder by contrast.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #46 and #48. Where #46 uses a blue field and angular, mask-like geometry with closed eyes, #47 shifts to a warm brown ground and a forward-facing expression with teeth and a dark mouth opening visible.

connections.reason: Both works layer dense multicolor lines over a single-color ground, but #46's blue field and closed X-marked eyes contrast directly with #47's brown ground and forward-facing expression with visible teeth.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye land first — on the white outline edge, the yellow-green irises, or the teeth — and what does that order suggest about how the image is organized?
ambiguities: The right side of the face dissolves into darker, looser marks that may indicate a second partial form or simply edge treatment; the image alone does not resolve this.
